source.title: Mechanistic Personality Analysis of LLMs Steering Personality via Latent Feature Interventions

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE-based latent feature interventions to an LLM and reports effects on trait expression. It is a new setting relative to the toy-model superposition claim; it does not reproduce the toy-model experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports personality-evaluation outcomes after feature interventions, which bear on V4. Grid-search optima, feature counts, and shift magnitudes are not rows because they are used to select parameters. Its general performance and coherence results do not test the listed versions. Cited claims about toy-model superposition and SAE work are not treated as results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pretrained SAE (layer 19, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B) as a tool to steer personality traits. It reports only how well its steering method works: LLM and human detection rates and embedding cosine similarity. It does not measure whether the model stores features in superposition, whether neurons are polysemantic, or whether the SAE recovers the model's features. The trait expression is induced on purpose by feature shifts. The record's T3/tests classification is therefore wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE latent-feature steering modulates personality expression while maintaining performance, most reliably for Conscientiousness and Neuroticism. The 'compact' (Extraversion) vs 'distributed' (Openness) characterisation is inferred from grid-search optimal feature counts, i.e. tuning parameters, not from a representational measurement. They caveat that the SAE does not eliminate polysemanticity and that the effects are trait-associated language, not psychological traits.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive personality data, a pretrained SAE, and inference-time latent feature interventions in an LLM; it does not implement or reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by trait and evaluation method; positive and negative shifts also differ, with negative-shift cosine effects mixed across traits.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding weighted SAE decoder directions at layer 19 shifts judged trait expression strongly for Conscientiousness and Neuroticism, moderately for Extraversion and Agreeableness, and not for Openness (chance or below). Coherence collapses past a shift magnitude of about 20.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature directions in an LLM can be used to causally steer high-level behavioural or stylistic traits, with success varying by trait.

record.problems: Evidence is from one model and one SAE layer. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Embedding cosine is acknowledged by the authors as an incomplete measure, and human and LLM judgments differ for some traits. The paper notes that the SAE does not fully eliminate polysemanticity or guarantee alignment between its basis and trait structure.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweeps or feature geometry.
All: no capacity or feature-importance analysis.
All: no analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.

All: the SAE is assumed to recover features; there is no measurement of neuron-level distribution of features or of the SAE's recovery quality beyond the cited 93% L0 sparsity of a third-party checkpoint.
All: no tests of completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE features.
All: decoder directions are used but 1-D vs multi-dimensional features are not compared.

record.verdict_notes: This is a steering-method paper. Superposition and toy models appear only in the literature review. The record's V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels should be dropped: the rows measure the effectiveness of the authors' own intervention, not whether LLMs contain SAE-recoverable sparse features. The study is not an original source. No uncertainty estimates are given, and the 'correct' definition uses an >80% threshold, which is ambiguous against the reported percentages.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity, overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, and polysemanticity caused by limited capacity.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether it is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE feature interventions in one LLM on personality expression; does not measure general feature distribution across neurons, test other models, or establish broad recovery of model features.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Uses decoder feature vectors as directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated outputs after optimized positive and negative SAE feature shifts using LLM judgments of trait expression.

conditions.value: LLMs; Claude 3.7 and GPT-4o are named, results reported together

rows.measure: Percentage of evaluations in which judges correctly identified the trait-tuned response
rows.baseline: Untuned paired response; separate baseline rate not stated
rows.value: 94% correct
rows.note: Paper reports 200 trials of 20 evaluations per trait; no separate result by LLM judge is given.
rows.check: Steering-method performance (LLM-judge detection of trait-tuned text, 94%), not a measure of superposition or SAE feature recovery. Counts as 'correct' only above an 80% threshold; no chance baseline is stated.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Conscientiousness and Neuroticism; LLM and human judgments
reader_labels.reason: SAE feature interventions produced high reported detection rates for these traits (r1, r2, r6, r7), and positive shifts increased embedding similarity across traits (r11-r15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Extraversion and Agreeableness; Openness; negative shifts by trait
reader_labels.reason: Detection was weaker for Extraversion and Agreeableness and especially low for Openness (r3-r5, r8-r10); negative-shift cosine effects varied, were minimal for Agreeableness, and ran opposite to the expected direction for Openness (r16-r20).
